- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk premium or volatility.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; reduce forecast by 3–5% in the following 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, consider downward correction — especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If model forecast is <10% below recent 18-day average, consider upward adjustment — especially if sentiment is positive or rising.  
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 1–2 days; if sentiment turns positive, forecast should be adjusted up 1–2 days ahead, not just at the turn.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early period (days 1–5) when sentiment is rising; reduce early forecast by 1–3% to reflect momentum decay.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral or bearish), model underperforms; increase forecast by 2–4% to compensate for suppressed volatility.
